subject: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up — Foxtail AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex@foxtail.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming requirements (Foxtail)

Hi Alex — great demo today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything captured for the SLO/benchmark work:

Recap (what I heard today)
- Primary goal: embed streaming responses into customer chat UI with perceptually instant first token.
- Target TTFT: you mentioned aiming for sub-200ms in prod, ideally <=150ms for most traffic.
- Streaming approach: SSE is preferred today (server-sent events), WebSocket optional for future roadmap.
- Chunk/cadence: want small, frequent chunks — ~50–150ms cadence feels ideal; some responses may be multi-chunk.
- Concurrency/throughput: expected peak concurrency ~200 simultaneous users generating streaming responses, baseline qps ~40–60 requests/sec; burst to ~300 concurrency for events.
- Avg response size: ~100–150 tokens per response (user-facing short answers), some long-form (~800 tokens) in edge cases.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you confirm the hard TTFT target you want Redwood to design to (150ms or 200ms)?
2) Confirm SSE only vs WebSocket (we can support both; SSE has lower client complexity).
3) Share a sample traffic pattern (qps/median tokens/95p tokens) or a small dataset we can use for local perf runs.
4) I'll coordinate an internal perf run + benchmark against the targets and follow-up with dedicated capacity sizing and a short POC plan.

I've attached a short SLO worksheet and our TTFT SLO assumptions (redwood-ttft-slo.pdf). If Sam from procurement wants to be looped for timing/POC contracting, happy to include them.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-ttft-slo.pdf]

From: Alex Turner <alex@foxtail.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <procurement@foxtail.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming requirements (Foxtail)

Thanks Marissa — chat with the product team after our call and here are the clarified targets we can commit to for the POC:

- TTFT target: 150ms p50 for user-facing requests; p95 target we consider acceptable up to 300ms during bursts.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for v1. We'll evaluate WebSocket later if SSE limitations appear.
- Chunk cadence: target 50–100ms between chunks for typical responses. For very long outputs (>=500 tokens) we can relax cadence to 150–250ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 50 req/s with sustained concurrency of ~200. Peak/burst concurrency ~300 for short durations (1–5 min).
- Payload sizes: median 120 tokens, 95p ~620 tokens.

Attached is our procurement questionnaire and a small sample traces file (redacted). We'll get you a small synthetic trace with qps/token distribution by EOD.

Appreciate you running the perf — let us know what you need (SSE client test harness, sample prompts, auth).

—Alex
Alex Turner | Head of Product, Foxtail AI
[Attachment: foxtail-procurement-questions.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming requirements (Foxtail) — perf run ask

David/Neha — forwarding Alex's reply with the confirmed targets. Please see the asks below and advise on earliest ETA for an initial perf run.

Key targets from Foxtail:
- TTFT: 150ms p50, p95 up to 300ms during bursts
- Streaming via SSE, chunk cadence 50–100ms (150–250ms for >=500-token outputs)
- Baseline 50 req/s, concurrency ~200, peak burst ~300
- Median response ~120 tokens; 95p ~620 tokens

Perf run ask (initial scope)
- Run single-model inference with our streaming runtime using the sample trace Alex will provide. Measure TTFT and chunk cadence under load (50rps, 100rps, simulated concurrency ramp to 300).
- Capture p50/p95 TTFT, network latency breakdown, and chunk arrival distribution (inter-chunk times).
- Run both cold-start and warm (KV cache primed) scenarios where possible.
- Produce a short summary (1–2 pages) with recommended dedicated sizing (GPUs, batch config, cache settings) and any immediate red flags for hitting 150ms TTFT target.

Attachments: I've attached the SLO worksheet and the procurement doc. Alex / Sam — we'll treat the procurement doc as FYI while we work through perf sizing.

Thanks — please ack and give an ETA for the initial benchmark results.

Marissa
[Attachment: redwood-ttft-slo.pdf]

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming requirements (Foxtail) — perf run ask

Ack — pulling together a small benchmark plan. Initial notes:
- We'll start with the same model family used in demo (redwood-v2-medium) quantized FP16 path and run on a 4-GPU cluster to approximate dedicated capacity.
- Test matrix: 50rps, 100rps, 200rps sustained; concurrency ramps to 300 for 2 minutes. Measure TTFT p50/p95 and inter-chunk times.
- We'll include both SSE harness (headless client) and a simple WebSocket harness for comparison.
- ETA: first round of numbers and a one-page summary by EOD Friday (2026-03-27). Full sizing + recommendations early next week.

Neha — can you coordinate the sample trace ingestion and make sure the KV cache warm paths are scripted?

-David
